```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here("inst", "analysis"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
pacman::p_load(kableExtra, dplyr, tidyr, forcats, lme4, lmerTest, ggplot2, ggalluvial, cowplot, mixOmics, here, pheatmap)
devtools::load_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: import-results
#| include: false

## omics + visit design (needed to build X_diff) ##
omics_list <- readRDS(
  paste0("../../extdata/archive/DIABLO_X_list.rds")
)

patient_design <- readRDS(
  paste0("../../extdata/archive/DiffExp_Design_20230105.rds")
)

## load lca results (used to identify the outlier) ##
metformin_lca_2 <- readRDS(
  paste0("../../extdata/archive/Metformin.k2.LCA.NoOutlier.rds")
)

# Build X_diff via calculate_difference() so rows carry fxs_sts_id as names
X_diff <- list(
  Metabolites = calculate_difference(omics_list$compounds,  patient_data = patient_design),
  Lipids      = calculate_difference(omics_list$lipids,     patient_data = patient_design),
  Peptides    = calculate_difference(omics_list$proteins,   patient_data = patient_design),
  Proteomics  = calculate_difference(omics_list$proteomics, patient_data = patient_design)
)
X_diff <- lapply(X_diff, tibble::column_to_rownames, var = "fxs_sts_id")

# Remove the outlier: the subject absent from the NoOutlier LCA result
lca_ids    <- as.character(unique(metformin_lca_2$Data$id))
outlier_id <- setdiff(rownames(X_diff[[1]]), lca_ids)
if (length(outlier_id) == 1L) {
  message("Removing outlier: ", outlier_id)
  X_diff <- lapply(X_diff, function(m) m[rownames(m) != outlier_id, , drop = FALSE])
} else if (length(outlier_id) != 0L) {
  stop("Expected exactly one outlier; found: ", paste(outlier_id, collapse = ", "))
}

Y <- readRDS(
  file = paste0("../../extdata/archive/k2.Assignments.20230714.rds")
)

design.mat <- readRDS(
  file = "../../extdata/archive/Metformin.Difference.Diablo.Design.Matrix.rds"
)

rownames(design.mat) <- colnames(design.mat) <- c(
  "Metabolites", "Lipids", "Peptides", "Proteomics"
)

## load DIABLO results ##
k2.diablo.tune.final <- readRDS(
  paste0("../../extdata/archive/k2.DIABLO.Tuned.20230713.rds")
)




## Load repeated-measures phenotype data
phenotype.data <- readRDS(
  paste0("../../extdata/analytic_data_20260810.rds")
)

## Calculate all available phenotype differences (Visit 3 minus Visit 1)
## Note: age_group is non-numeric and does not change between visits, so we
## preserve it separately and rejoin after calculating differences
age_group_baseline <- phenotype.data |>
  dplyr::filter(redcap_event_name == "Baseline Visit (Visit 1)") |>
  dplyr::select(fxs_sts_id, age_group)

phenotype.data.diff <- phenotype.data |>
  dplyr::select(-age_group) |>
  calculate_phenotype_diff(id_col = "fxs_sts_id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(age_group_baseline, by = "fxs_sts_id")

# Align phenotype block to SNF participants; Treatment retained for summaries only
snf_ids <- rownames(X_diff[[1]])
missing_phenotype_ids <- setdiff(
  snf_ids,
  as.character(phenotype.data.diff$fxs_sts_id)
)
if (length(missing_phenotype_ids) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Phenotype differences are missing for SNF participant(s): ",
    paste(missing_phenotype_ids, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Exclude NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery and Facial-emotion processing from SNF
phenotype_snf_exclude_cols <- c(
  "tcb_flnkr_analytic", "tcb_dccs_analytic", "tcb_vocb_analytic",
  "tcb_ptrncomp_analytic", "tcb_lstsrt_analytic",
  "tcb_picseq_analytic", "tcb_read_analytic",
  "tcb_spdmtch_analytic", "tcb_crystl_analytic",
  "tcb_earlycomp_analytic", "tcb_cogcomp_analytic",
  "tcb_fluid_analytic",
  "Happy_Eyes_Pct", "Happy_Nose_Pct", "Happy_Mouth_Pct",
  "Fear_Eyes_Pct", "Fear_Nose_Pct", "Fear_Mouth_Pct",
  "Calm_Eyes_Pct", "Calm_Nose_Pct", "Calm_Mouth_Pct",
  "All_Face_Pct_vP"
)

phenotype_snf_data <- phenotype.data.diff |>
  dplyr::mutate(fxs_sts_id = as.character(fxs_sts_id)) |>
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(phenotype_snf_exclude_cols)) |>
  na.omit()
```

# Part 1: Previous LCA & DIABLO Analysis

## 1.1 LCA Clustering

```{r}
#| label: avg-response-by-cluster
lca_2_means <- data.frame(
  "Cluster" = as.factor(c(rep(c(1, 2), each = 3))),
  "Visit" = rep(c(1, 2, 3), 2),
  "ABC.Composite" = c(
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 3,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "abc_comp_rev"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "abc_comp_rev"] * 3
  ),
  "ADAMS.Total" = c(
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 3,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "ADAMS_Total"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "ADAMS_Total"] * 3
  ),
  "PedsQL" = c(
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 3,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 1,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 2,
    metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["int", "PedsQL"] + 
      metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest_mean["visit", "PedsQL"] * 3
  )
) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ABC.Composite, ADAMS.Total, PedsQL),
               names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Score") |>
  mutate(
    y_min = 0,
    y_max = case_when(
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" ~ 80,
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total" ~ 40,
      Measure == "PedsQL" ~ 300
    )
  )

# average Std Error
lca_2_ste <- data.frame(
  Cluster = c(1, 2),
  ABC.Composite = c(
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[1]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[2]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"])
    ),
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[1]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[2]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"])
    )
  ),
  ADAMS.Total = c(
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[1]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[3]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"])
    ),
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[1]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[3]]["visit1_", "Std. Error"])
    )
  ),
  PedsQL = c(
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[2]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`1`$Fixedest[[3]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"])
    ),
    mean(
      c(metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[2]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"],
        metformin_lca_2$Models$`2`$Fixedest[[3]]["visit2_", "Std. Error"])
    )
  )
)

# add +/- 1.96*StdError
test <- lca_2_means |>
  mutate(
    seg.min = case_when(
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" & Cluster == 1 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "ABC.Composite"]),
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total"  & Cluster == 1 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "ADAMS.Total"]),
      Measure == "PedsQL"  & Cluster == 1 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "PedsQL"]),
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" & Cluster == 2 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "ABC.Composite"]),
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total"  & Cluster == 2 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "ADAMS.Total"]),
      Measure == "PedsQL"  & Cluster == 2 ~ Score - (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "PedsQL"])
    ),
    seg.max = case_when(
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" & Cluster == 1 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "ABC.Composite"]),
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total"  & Cluster == 1 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "ADAMS.Total"]),
      Measure == "PedsQL"  & Cluster == 1 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["1", "PedsQL"]),
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" & Cluster == 2 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "ABC.Composite"]),
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total"  & Cluster == 2 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "ADAMS.Total"]),
      Measure == "PedsQL"  & Cluster == 2 ~ Score + (1.96 * lca_2_ste["2", "PedsQL"])
    )
  )

# rename variables for figures
test <- test |>
  mutate(
    Measure = case_when(
      Measure == "ABC.Composite" ~ "ABC Composite Score",
      Measure == "ADAMS.Total" ~ "ADAMS Total",
      Measure == "PedsQL" ~ "Pediatric Quality of Life"
    )
  )
```

# Part 2: LCA Clusters vs. Treatment Groups

Now that the clinical trial has completed, how do our LCA cluster assignments 
compare to our Treatment groups?  

```{r}
compare_clusters <- metformin_lca_2$Data |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    x = _,
    y = lca.diablo::unblinding_key |> dplyr::select(fxs_sts_id, unmasked),
    by = c("id" = "fxs_sts_id")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::select(id, cluster, unmasked) |> 
  dplyr::distinct()

compare_clusters |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = unmasked,
    col = cluster,
    label = list(
      unmasked ~ "Treatment Group",
      cluster ~ "LCA Cluster"
    )
  )
```

## 2.1 Patient Characteristics by Subgroup

```{r}
subgroup_data <- compare_clusters |> 
  dplyr::left_join(
    x = _,
    y = lca.diablo::redcap_data |> 
      dplyr::filter(redcap_event_name == "baseline_visit_vis_arm_1"),
    by = c("id" = "fxs_sts_id")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    Subgroup = glue::glue("{unmasked}, {cluster}") |> 
      factor(
        levels = c(
          "Metformin, 1", "Metformin, 2",
          "Placebo, 1", "Placebo, 2"
        )
      ),
    Age = demo_age |> as.numeric(),
    tassone_cat = tassone_cat |> toupper(),
    `Age Category` = dplyr::case_when(
      Age < 12 ~ "6-11 yrs",
      Age >= 12 ~ "12+ yrs"
    ) |> 
      factor(levels = c("6-11 yrs", "12+ yrs"))
  )

subgroup_data |> 
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    by = Subgroup,
    type = Age ~ "continuous2",
    statistic = Age ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", 
                        "{median} ({p25}, {p75})", 
                        "{min}, {max}"),
    include = c(Age, `Age Category`, tassone_cat)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_overall()
```

# Part 3: Similarity Network Fusion (SNF) Consensus Subtypes

### Methodology

SNF (Wang et al. 2014, *Nature Methods* 11, 333–337) finds subtypes from four
V3 minus V1 omics change-score blocks: metabolites, lipids, peptides, and
proteomics. Clustering itself never sees treatment group, but preprocessing
uses the Placebo group as a reference for standardization:

- **Feature selection** — keep the top 100 most variable features per block
  (MAD, median absolute deviation).
- **Normalization** — Z-score each block using Placebo subjects as the
  reference (center and scale computed from Placebo group, applied to all
  subjects).

**Why:** using Placebo as the reference provides a stable baseline for
comparing Metformin-treated subjects against a control standard, ensuring
that any SNF-subtype × Treatment-group associations reflect genuine biological
differences rather than arbitrary scaling choices.

**Steps:** feature selection (MAD) → normalization (Z-score with Placebo
reference) → per-block affinity (`SNFtool::affinityMatrix`) → network fusion
(`SNFtool::SNF`) → cluster-number selection (Eigen-gap,
`estimateNumberOfClustersGivenGraph`) → final clustering
(`SNFtool::spectralClustering`).

### SNF Subtyping by Multi-Omic

```{r}
#| include: false

# Extract Placebo IDs to use as reference for Z-score normalization
placebo_ids <- compare_clusters |>
  dplyr::filter(unmasked == "Placebo") |>
  dplyr::pull(id) |>
  as.character()

control_ids <- intersect(rownames(X_diff[[1]]), placebo_ids)

# SAP Step 2: unsupervised data reduction — retain the top 100 features per
# block by dispersion (MAD), with NO reference to treatment group.
# SAP Step 3: normalize each block using Placebo subjects as the reference
# (center and scale computed from Placebo group, applied to all subjects).
# SAP Step 4: preliminary SNF to obtain fused network for cluster estimation
snf_prelim <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = X_diff,
  n_clusters               = 2,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad",
  control_ids              = if (length(control_ids) >= 2) control_ids else NULL
)

# SAP Step 4: data-driven cluster number selection (Eigen-gap criterion)
n_clust_est         <- SNFtool::estimateNumberOfClustersGivenGraph(
  W = snf_prelim$fused_network, NUMC = 2:8
)
n_clusters_selected <- n_clust_est[[1]]

# Final SNF with data-selected number of clusters
snf_fit <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = X_diff,
  n_clusters               = n_clusters_selected,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad",
  control_ids              = if (length(control_ids) >= 2) control_ids else NULL
)
```

The Eigen-gap criterion suggests **`r n_clusters_selected`** cluster(s)
(Rotation cost criterion: `r n_clust_est[[2]]`).
Top 100 features per block were retained by dispersion (median absolute
deviation), independent of treatment group.
Each block was Z-scored using Placebo subjects as the reference, with
center and scale parameters computed from the Placebo group and applied to
all subjects.

```{r}
snf_annotations <- annotate_snf_subtypes(
  subtypes = snf_fit$subtypes,
  clinical_data = compare_clusters |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)),
  id_col = "id"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    snf_subtype = factor(snf_subtype)
  )

snf_annotations |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = unmasked,
    col = snf_subtype,
    label = list(
      unmasked ~ "Treatment Group",
      snf_subtype ~ "SNF Subtype"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "SNF Fused Similarity Network — click to enlarge"
#|   width: 14
#|   height: 12
snf_order <- order(snf_fit$subtypes)
ordered_ids <- rownames(snf_fit$fused_network)[snf_order]
ordered_annotations <- snf_annotations |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
  dplyr::slice(match(ordered_ids, id))

subtype_levels <- ordered_annotations$snf_subtype |>
  droplevels() |>
  levels()
subtype_palette <- stats::setNames(
  scales::hue_pal()(length(subtype_levels)),
  subtype_levels
)
treatment_levels <- c("Metformin", "Placebo")
treatment_palette <- stats::setNames(
  scales::hue_pal(l = 45)(length(treatment_levels)),
  treatment_levels
)

# Build annotation data frames for pheatmap (rows = subjects, ordered by subtype)
snf_annot <- data.frame(
  `SNF Subtype`      = ordered_annotations$snf_subtype,
  `Treatment Group`  = ordered_annotations$unmasked,
  row.names          = ordered_annotations$id,
  check.names        = FALSE
)
snf_annot_colors <- list(
  `SNF Subtype`     = subtype_palette,
  `Treatment Group` = treatment_palette
)

# Data-driven color breaks (1st–99th percentile) to avoid washout
fused_mat  <- snf_fit$fused_network[snf_order, snf_order]
fused_vals <- fused_mat[upper.tri(fused_mat)]
fused_breaks <- seq(quantile(fused_vals, 0.01),
                    quantile(fused_vals, 0.99),
                    length.out = 101)
fused_cols <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
  c("#f7fbff", "#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#2171b5", "#08306b")  # Blues (5-stop)
)(100)

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  fused_mat,
  color             = fused_cols,
  breaks            = fused_breaks,
  annotation_row    = snf_annot,
  annotation_col    = snf_annot,
  annotation_colors = snf_annot_colors,
  cluster_rows      = FALSE,   # already ordered by subtype
  cluster_cols      = FALSE,
  show_rownames     = TRUE,
  show_colnames     = TRUE,
  cellwidth         = 10,      # fixed cell size so figure auto-expands
  cellheight        = 10,
  fontsize          = 10,      # base font (legend, axis titles)
  fontsize_row      = 9,
  fontsize_col      = 9,
  angle_col         = 90,
  border_color      = NA,
  main              = "SNF Fused Similarity Network"
)
```

#### Multi-Omic Similarity Network

The network displays the strongest 5% of participant-to-participant
similarities from the fused multi-omic network. Node color identifies the
multi-omic subtype, node shape identifies treatment group, and edge opacity
represents similarity strength.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Multi-omic similarity network — click to enlarge"

multiomic_affinity <- snf_fit$fused_network
multiomic_edge_values <- multiomic_affinity[upper.tri(multiomic_affinity)]
multiomic_edge_threshold <- stats::quantile(
  multiomic_edge_values,
  probs = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

multiomic_network_matrix <- multiomic_affinity
multiomic_network_matrix[
  multiomic_network_matrix < multiomic_edge_threshold
] <- 0
diag(multiomic_network_matrix) <- 0

multiomic_network <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  multiomic_network_matrix,
  mode = "undirected",
  weighted = TRUE,
  diag = FALSE
)

snf_annotations_lookup <- snf_annotations |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))

multiomic_annotation_idx <- match(
  igraph::V(multiomic_network)$name,
  snf_annotations_lookup$id
)

# Drop any network vertices without a matching multi-omic subtype
# annotation, so vertex attributes stay aligned with the graph.
multiomic_network_dropped <- igraph::V(multiomic_network)$name[
  is.na(multiomic_annotation_idx)
]
if (length(multiomic_network_dropped) > 0L) {
  message(
    "Dropping participant(s) without multi-omic subtype annotations from the network: ",
    paste(multiomic_network_dropped, collapse = ", ")
  )
  multiomic_network <- igraph::delete_vertices(
    multiomic_network,
    which(is.na(multiomic_annotation_idx))
  )
  multiomic_annotation_idx <- multiomic_annotation_idx[
    !is.na(multiomic_annotation_idx)
  ]
}

multiomic_network_annotations <- snf_annotations_lookup |>
  dplyr::slice(multiomic_annotation_idx)

multiomic_network <- multiomic_network |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "snf_subtype",
    value = multiomic_network_annotations$snf_subtype
  ) |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "treatment_group",
    value = multiomic_network_annotations$unmasked
  )

set.seed(4328)
multiomic_fr_layout <- igraph::layout_with_fr(multiomic_network)
multiomic_network_layout <- ggnetwork::ggnetwork(
  multiomic_network,
  layout = multiomic_fr_layout,
  weights = igraph::E(multiomic_network)$weight
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  multiomic_network_layout,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
) +
  ggnetwork::geom_edges(
    ggplot2::aes(linewidth = weight),
    colour = "grey55",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnetwork::geom_nodes(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = snf_subtype,
      shape = treatment_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = subtype_palette,
    name = "SNF Subtype"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(21, 24),
    name = "Treatment Group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black")
    ),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = "grey50")
    )
  ) +
  ggnetwork::theme_blank() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Fused similarity network") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

#### Top Feature Contributions per Domain (NMI)

Following the feature-ranking approach from the KCNI SNF tutorial
(`rankFeaturesByNMI()`), each block's features (after the same MAD
selection/Z-scoring used to build the fused network) are ranked by
Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) with the fused-network subtypes. This
identifies which features within each omics domain contribute most to the
discovered subtypes, independent of treatment group.

```{r}
#| label: nmi-feature-ranking

# rankFeaturesByNMI() returns list(NMI.scores, NMI.ranks): each element is a
# plain vector aligned to the columns of the corresponding block (score/rank
# per feature), NOT a feature-index/value matrix.
nmi_result <- SNFtool::rankFeaturesByNMI(
  data = snf_fit$processed_omics,
  W    = snf_fit$fused_network
)

nmi_top_n     <- 10
domain_names  <- names(snf_fit$processed_omics)

top_features_by_domain <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(domain_names), function(i) {
  domain    <- domain_names[i]
  mat       <- snf_fit$processed_omics[[i]]
  nmi_score <- nmi_result[[1]][[i]]
  feat_idx  <- order(nmi_score, decreasing = TRUE)
  n_take    <- min(nmi_top_n, length(feat_idx))
  feat_idx  <- feat_idx[seq_len(n_take)]

  data.frame(
    Domain  = domain,
    Rank    = seq_len(n_take),
    Feature = colnames(mat)[feat_idx],
    NMI     = nmi_score[feat_idx]
  )
}))

top_features_by_domain |>
  kableExtra::kbl(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Top features per domain, ranked by NMI with fused-network subtypes"
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Top feature NMI by domain — click to enlarge"

top_features_by_domain |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Feature = forcats::fct_reorder(Feature, NMI)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Feature, y = NMI, fill = Domain)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Domain, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Normalized Mutual Information (with fused-network subtypes)",
    title = "Top Feature Contributions per Domain"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
# Helper: extract Visit 1 data for one omics block, join subgroup labels
prepare_omics_v1 <- function(block_mat) {
  block_mat |>
    tibble::as_tibble(rownames = NA) |>

    dplyr::left_join(
      patient_design |> dplyr::select(fxs_sts_id, Visit1),

    dplyr::select(-flora_id)
```

#### Phenotype Changes by SNF Subtype

This section uses all available phenotype change scores from
`analytic_data.rds`. Each change is calculated as **Visit 3 − Visit 1** and
is left on its original scale. Consequently, the direction of a favorable
change depends on the instrument: lower scores are generally favorable for
ABC, ADAMS, SNAP-IV, and target-behavior severity, whereas higher scores are
generally favorable for language, PedsQL, Vineland-3, and cognition measures.
Facial-emotion processing outcomes are descriptive and do not have a single
favorable direction. Summaries are shown separately by SNF subtype and
treatment group. No SNF subtype × treatment interaction groups or interaction
terms are used. Because phenotype changes contribute to subtype construction,
the subtype-stratified phenotype results characterize the discovered subtypes;
their p-values are exploratory rather than independent confirmatory tests.

```{r}
# Build one SNF block per clinical domain. The NIH Toolbox and facial-emotion
# domains are not present here because they were excluded from
# `phenotype_snf_data` upstream.
make_phenotype_snf_blocks <- function(data, domains) {
  blocks <- lapply(
    domains,
    function(domain_measures) {
      measures <- intersect(domain_measures, names(data))
      measures <- measures[
        vapply(
          data[measures],
          function(x) {
            is.numeric(x) && sum(!is.na(x)) >= 2L &&
              is.finite(stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)) &&
              stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
          },
          logical(1)
        )
      ]

      if (length(measures) == 0L) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      block <- as.matrix(data[, measures, drop = FALSE])
      storage.mode(block) <- "double"
      rownames(block) <- as.character(data$fxs_sts_id)
      block
    }
  )

  blocks <- Filter(Negate(is.null), blocks)
  if (length(blocks) < 2L) {
    stop("At least two informative phenotype domains are required for SNF.")
  }

  blocks
}

combine_phenotype_snf_blocks <- function(processed_omics) {
  do.call(cbind, processed_omics)
}

order_heatmap_rows_by_subtype <- function(mat, annotation, subtype_col) {
  if (!subtype_col %in% names(annotation)) {
    stop("Subtype annotation column is missing from the heatmap annotations.")
  }
  if (is.null(rownames(mat)) || is.null(rownames(annotation)) ||
      !setequal(rownames(mat), rownames(annotation))) {
    stop("Heatmap matrix and annotation participant IDs do not match.")
  }

  annotation <- annotation[rownames(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  subtype <- droplevels(factor(annotation[[subtype_col]]))
  if (anyNA(subtype)) {
    stop("Subtype annotations are missing for at least one heatmap row.")
  }

  subtype_levels <- levels(subtype)
  within_subtype_order <- lapply(
    subtype_levels,
    function(level) {
      idx <- which(subtype == level)
      if (length(idx) <= 1L) {
        return(idx)
      }

      idx[stats::hclust(stats::dist(mat[idx, , drop = FALSE]))$order]
    }
  )
  row_order <- unlist(within_subtype_order, use.names = FALSE)
  subtype_sizes <- vapply(
    subtype_levels,
    function(level) sum(subtype == level),
    integer(1)
  )
  gaps_row <- if (length(subtype_sizes) > 1L) {
    utils::head(cumsum(subtype_sizes), -1L)
  } else {
    integer(0)
  }

  list(
    matrix = mat[row_order, , drop = FALSE],
    annotation = annotation[row_order, , drop = FALSE],
    gaps_row = gaps_row
  )
}

#' Draw a k=2-to-k=3 phenotype-subtype Sankey diagram
#'
#' @param sankey_data Long-format subtype assignments for each classification.
#' @param base_size Base font size for the plot theme.
#' @param plot_title Plot title.
#' @return A [ggplot2::ggplot] Sankey diagram.
#' @keywords internal
#' @noRd
draw_subtype_sankey <- function(
  sankey_data,
  base_size = 11,
  plot_title = "Phenotype subtype assignments: k = 2 versus k = 3"
) {
  classification_levels <- c("k = 2", "k = 3")
  subtype_levels <- c("Subtype 1", "Subtype 2", "Subtype 3")
  subtype_colours <- stats::setNames(
    scales::hue_pal()(length(subtype_levels)),
    subtype_levels
  )
  sankey_mapping <- ggplot2::aes(
    x = .data$classification,
    stratum = .data$subtype,
    alluvium = .data$id,
    y = 1
  )

  ggplot2::ggplot(sankey_data, sankey_mapping) +
    ggalluvial::geom_flow(
      ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$subtype),
      aes.flow = "backward",
      alpha = 0.75,
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 0.15,
      outline.type = "full",
      width = 1 / 12,
      reverse = TRUE
    ) +
    ggalluvial::geom_stratum(
      ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$subtype),
      alpha = 1,
      colour = "grey35",
      linewidth = 0.35,
      width = 1 / 8,
      reverse = TRUE
    ) +
    ggalluvial::stat_stratum(
      geom = "label",
      ggplot2::aes(
        label = paste0(
          ggplot2::after_stat(.data$stratum), "\n",
          ggplot2::after_stat(count), " (",
          round(100 * ggplot2::after_stat(.data$prop)), "%)"
        )
      ),
      colour = "grey10",
      fill = "white",
      alpha = 0.9,
      linewidth = 0.2,
      size = 3,
      reverse = TRUE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
      limits = classification_levels,
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0.02, add = 0.35)
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = subtype_colours,
      breaks = subtype_levels,
      drop = FALSE,
      name = "Phenotype subtype"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Participants",
      title = plot_title,
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Each band follows one participant; band colour shows the k = 3 destination subtype.\n",
        "Widths represent participants; labels show n (percent)."
      ),
      caption = paste(
        "These are alternative classifications of the same cohort, not longitudinal transitions.",
        "Subtype numbers are arbitrary labels."
      )
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

rank_phenotype_snf_features <- function(snf_fit) {
  nmi_result <- SNFtool::rankFeaturesByNMI(
    data = snf_fit$processed_omics,
    W = snf_fit$fused_network
  )
  nmi_scores <- nmi_result[[1]]
  blocks <- snf_fit$processed_omics

  if (length(nmi_scores) != length(blocks)) {
    stop("NMI output does not match the number of phenotype-domain blocks.")
  }

  feature_scores <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(
      seq_along(blocks),
      function(i) {
        features <- colnames(blocks[[i]])
        scores <- as.numeric(nmi_scores[[i]])
        if (length(features) != length(scores)) {
          stop("NMI score count does not match the features in a phenotype domain.")
        }
        data.frame(
          Domain = names(blocks)[[i]],
          Feature = features,
          NMI = scores,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    )
  )

  feature_scores |>
    dplyr::group_by(Domain) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(NMI), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      n_vars = dplyr::n(),
      top_n = ifelse(n_vars > 3L, 3L, 1L)
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::row_number() <= top_n) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Rank = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::mutate(Domain = factor(Domain, levels = names(blocks))) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Domain, Rank) |>
    dplyr::select(Domain, Rank, Feature, NMI)
}

phenotype_snf_blocks <- make_phenotype_snf_blocks(
  data = phenotype_snf_data,
  domains = phenotype_domains
)

phenotype_analysis <- phenotype.data.diff |>
  dplyr::mutate(fxs_sts_id = as.character(fxs_sts_id)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    snf_annotations |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        fxs_sts_id = as.character(id),
        snf_subtype,
        unmasked
      ),
    by = "fxs_sts_id"
  )

treatment_mismatch <- with(
  phenotype_analysis,
  !is.na(Treatment) & !is.na(unmasked) &
    as.character(Treatment) != as.character(unmasked)
)
if (any(treatment_mismatch)) {
  stop("Treatment assignments differ between phenotype and SNF annotations.")
}

phenotype_analysis <- phenotype_analysis |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(snf_subtype)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Treatment = factor(
      as.character(Treatment),
      levels = c("Metformin", "Placebo")
    ),
    snf_subtype = droplevels(factor(snf_subtype))
  )

phenotype_analysis <- phenotype_analysis |>
  dplyr::select(-unmasked)

for (variable in phenotype_measure_cols) {
  if (!variable %in% names(phenotype_analysis)) {
    next
  }
  variable_label <- attr(
    phenotype.data.diff[[variable]],
    "label",
    exact = TRUE
  )
  if (is.null(variable_label) || !nzchar(variable_label)) {
    variable_label <- if (variable %in% names(phenotype_label_fallback)) {
      phenotype_label_fallback[[variable]]
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(variable_label)) {
    attr(phenotype_analysis[[variable]], "label") <- paste0(
      variable_label,
      " (V3 - V1)"
    )
  }
}

make_phenotype_summary <- function(data, by, domains, include_p = FALSE) {
  domain_tables <- lapply(
    domains,
    function(domain) {
      measures <- phenotype_domains[[domain]]
      measures <- measures[
        vapply(
          data[measures],
          function(x) any(!is.na(x)),
          logical(1)
        )
      ]

      summary_data <- data |>
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(by, measures)))

      # Character grouping avoids incompatible factor levels when an outcome
      # is entirely missing within one subgroup.
      summary_data[[by]] <- as.character(summary_data[[by]])

      summary_table <- summary_data |>
        gtsummary::tbl_summary(
          by = dplyr::all_of(by),
          include = dplyr::all_of(measures),
          type = dplyr::all_of(measures) ~ "continuous2",
          statistic = dplyr::all_of(measures) ~
            c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median} ({p25}, {p75})"),
          digits = dplyr::all_of(measures) ~ 1,
          missing = "ifany"
        )

      if (include_p) {
        summary_table <- summary_table |>
          gtsummary::add_p()
      }

      summary_table |>
        gtsummary::add_overall(last = TRUE)
    }
  )

  gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = domain_tables,
    group_header = domains
  )
}

phenotype_dictionary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(
    names(phenotype_domains),
    function(domain) {
      data.frame(
        Domain = factor(domain, levels = names(phenotype_domains)),
        Variable = phenotype_domains[[domain]],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

phenotype_coverage <- phenotype_dictionary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Paired N` = vapply(
      Variable,
      function(variable) sum(!is.na(phenotype_analysis[[variable]])),
      integer(1)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Domain) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Outcomes available` = sum(`Paired N` > 0L),
    `Paired N, median (range)` = sprintf(
      "%.0f (%d-%d)",
      stats::median(`Paired N`[`Paired N` > 0L]),
      min(`Paired N`[`Paired N` > 0L]),
      max(`Paired N`[`Paired N` > 0L])
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

The table below reports the paired sample size after restricting the
phenotype data to participants included in the SNF analysis. Outcomes with no
paired Visit 1 and Visit 3 values are omitted from subsequent tables.

```{r tab.cap="Phenotype Data Coverage"}
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "c", "c")) |>
  kableExtra::kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r tab.cap="Behavior, Quality of Life, and Language by SNF"}
)
```

# Part 4: Phenotype-Based Similarity Network Fusion

Phenotype change scores are represented as one input block per retained clinical
domain. `run_snf_subtypes()` constructs an affinity matrix for each domain and
then fuses those participant-similarity networks with `SNFtool::SNF()` before
spectral clustering. Feature selection and normalization are label-free.

```{r}
#| include: false

# SAP Step 2: retain up to the top 100 features within each clinical-domain
# block by dispersion (MAD), with no reference to treatment group.
# SAP Step 3: normalize each domain block against all subjects so treatment
# assignment never enters the clustering input through centering or scaling.
# SAP Step 4: preliminary SNF to obtain a fused network for cluster estimation
snf_prelim_phenotype <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = phenotype_snf_blocks,
  n_clusters               = 2,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad"
)

# SAP Step 4: data-driven cluster number selection (Eigen-gap criterion)
n_clust_est_phenotype         <- SNFtool::estimateNumberOfClustersGivenGraph(
  W = snf_prelim_phenotype$fused_network, NUMC = 2:8
)
n_clusters_selected_phenotype <- n_clust_est_phenotype[[1]]

# Final run with data-selected number of clusters
snf_fit_phenotype <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = phenotype_snf_blocks,
  n_clusters               = n_clusters_selected_phenotype,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad"
)
```

The Eigen-gap criterion suggests **`r n_clusters_selected_phenotype`**
cluster(s) (Rotation cost criterion: `r n_clust_est_phenotype[[2]]`).
Within each retained clinical domain, up to 100 features are selected by
median absolute deviation without reference to treatment. Each domain block is
Z-scored across all subjects before the domain-specific affinity networks are
fused, keeping subtype discovery label-free.

```{r}
# Join phenotype subtypes to the full phenotype-clustering cohort
# (`phenotype_snf_data`, ~all participants with complete phenotype change
# scores), NOT the 24-participant multi-omics `compare_clusters` cohort.
# `compare_clusters` is restricted to participants with complete
# metabolomics/lipidomics/peptide/proteomics profiling (the original LCA +
# DIABLO sub-study), which is unrelated to phenotype data completeness.
# Joining phenotype subtypes onto `compare_clusters` would silently drop
# every phenotype-clustered participant outside that 24-person cohort from
# this table, Section 4.1's heatmap, and Section 4.2's network — even
# though the clustering itself (`snf_fit_phenotype`, above) already runs on
# the full phenotype cohort. The 24-person multi-omics restriction is
# reintroduced only in Section 4.3, where comparing phenotype subtypes to
# multi-omic subtypes requires participants present in both analyses.
phenotype_clinical_ids <- phenotype_snf_data |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = fxs_sts_id,
    unmasked = Treatment
  )

snf_annotations_phenotype <- annotate_snf_subtypes(
  subtypes = snf_fit_phenotype$subtypes,
  clinical_data = phenotype_clinical_ids,
  id_col = "id"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    snf_subtype_phenotype = factor(snf_subtype)
  )

snf_annotations_phenotype |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = unmasked,
    col = snf_subtype_phenotype,
    label = list(
      unmasked ~ "Treatment Group",
      snf_subtype_phenotype ~ "Phenotype Subtype"
    )
  )
```

## 4.1 Phenotype Change Heatmap by Subgroup

The heatmap displays the domain-specific phenotype change-score blocks used for
SNF. Values are standardized within outcome across participants. The phenotype
SNF cohort uses complete-case filtering (`na.omit()`), so participants with
missing retained phenotype data are excluded rather than imputed.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype change heatmap - click to enlarge"

phenotype_heatmap_matrix <- combine_phenotype_snf_blocks(
  snf_fit_phenotype$processed_omics
)

phenotype_heatmap_annotations <- snf_annotations_phenotype |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
  dplyr::slice(match(rownames(phenotype_heatmap_matrix), id))

if (anyNA(phenotype_heatmap_annotations$id)) {
  stop("Phenotype heatmap annotations are missing for at least one participant.")
}

phenotype_heatmap_annot <- data.frame(
  `Phenotype Subtype` = phenotype_heatmap_annotations$snf_subtype_phenotype,
  `Treatment Group` = phenotype_heatmap_annotations$unmasked,
  row.names = phenotype_heatmap_annotations$id,
  check.names = FALSE
)

phenotype_subtype_levels <- phenotype_heatmap_annot[["Phenotype Subtype"]] |>
  droplevels() |>
  levels()
phenotype_subtype_palette <- stats::setNames(
  scales::hue_pal()(length(phenotype_subtype_levels)),
  phenotype_subtype_levels
)
phenotype_heatmap_display <- order_heatmap_rows_by_subtype(
  mat = phenotype_heatmap_matrix,
  annotation = phenotype_heatmap_annot,
  subtype_col = "Phenotype Subtype"
)

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  phenotype_heatmap_display$matrix,
  color = omics_col_pal,
  annotation_row = phenotype_heatmap_display$annotation,
  annotation_colors = list(
    `Phenotype Subtype` = phenotype_subtype_palette,
    `Treatment Group` = treatment_palette
  ),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  gaps_row = phenotype_heatmap_display$gaps_row,
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize = 10,
  fontsize_row = 9,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Phenotype Changes (Visit 3 - Visit 1), Z-scored"
)
```

## 4.2 Phenotype Similarity Network

The network displays the strongest 5% of participant-to-participant
similarities from the phenotype affinity matrix. Node color identifies the
phenotype-derived subtype, node shape identifies treatment group, and edge
opacity represents similarity strength.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype similarity network — click to enlarge"

phenotype_affinity <- snf_fit_phenotype$fused_network
phenotype_edge_values <- phenotype_affinity[upper.tri(phenotype_affinity)]
phenotype_edge_threshold <- stats::quantile(
  phenotype_edge_values,
  probs = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_network_matrix <- phenotype_affinity
phenotype_network_matrix[
  phenotype_network_matrix < phenotype_edge_threshold
] <- 0
diag(phenotype_network_matrix) <- 0

phenotype_network <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  phenotype_network_matrix,
  mode = "undirected",
  weighted = TRUE,
  diag = FALSE
)

snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup <- snf_annotations_phenotype |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))

# `dplyr::slice(match(...))` silently drops rows for any unmatched vertex
# name instead of producing an NA row, which would desync the annotations
# from the graph's vertex count. Explicitly drop any network vertices that
# lack a matching phenotype-subtype annotation (e.g. participants excluded
# from phenotype-based clustering by `na.omit()` upstream) before assigning
# vertex attributes, so the two stay aligned.
phenotype_annotation_idx <- match(
  igraph::V(phenotype_network)$name,
  snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup$id
)

phenotype_network_dropped <- igraph::V(phenotype_network)$name[
  is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx)
]
if (length(phenotype_network_dropped) > 0L) {
  message(
    "Dropping participant(s) without phenotype subtype annotations from the network: ",
    paste(phenotype_network_dropped, collapse = ", ")
  )
  phenotype_network <- igraph::delete_vertices(
    phenotype_network,
    which(is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx))
  )
  phenotype_annotation_idx <- phenotype_annotation_idx[
    !is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx)
  ]
}

phenotype_network_annotations <- snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup |>
  dplyr::slice(phenotype_annotation_idx)

phenotype_network <- phenotype_network |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "phenotype_subtype",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations$snf_subtype_phenotype
  ) |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "treatment_group",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations$unmasked
  )

set.seed(4328)
fr_layout <- igraph::layout_with_fr(phenotype_network)
phenotype_network_layout <- ggnetwork::ggnetwork(
  phenotype_network,
  layout = fr_layout,
  weights = igraph::E(phenotype_network)$weight
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  phenotype_network_layout,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
) +
  ggnetwork::geom_edges(
    ggplot2::aes(linewidth = weight),
    colour = "grey55",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnetwork::geom_nodes(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = phenotype_subtype,
      shape = treatment_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = phenotype_subtype_palette,
    name = "Phenotype Subtype"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(21, 24),
    name = "Treatment Group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black")
    ),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = "grey50")
    )
  ) +
  ggnetwork::theme_blank() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Fused similarity network") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

## 4.3 Multi-Omics and Phenotype Classification Comparison

The two subtype assignments are joined by participant ID and combined into
cross-classified rows. Treatment groups are displayed in columns. Subtype
numbers are arbitrary labels, so equally numbered multi-omic and phenotype
subtypes should not be assumed to represent the same group.

```{r}
multiomic_classification <- snf_annotations |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    snf_subtype_multiomic = droplevels(factor(snf_subtype)),
    treatment_group = droplevels(factor(unmasked))
  )

phenotype_classification <- snf_annotations_phenotype |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    snf_subtype_phenotype = droplevels(factor(snf_subtype_phenotype))
  )

if (anyDuplicated(multiomic_classification$id) ||
    anyDuplicated(phenotype_classification$id)) {
  stop("Each classification must contain one row per participant.")
}

# Participants with any missing phenotype change score are excluded from
# phenotype-based clustering (see the `na.omit()` step above), so the two
# classifications need not contain identical participant sets. Only
# participants present in both are compared below.
phenotype_only_dropped <- setdiff(
  multiomic_classification$id,
  phenotype_classification$id
)

snf_classification_comparison <- multiomic_classification |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    phenotype_classification,
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cross_classification = factor(
      paste0(
        "Multi-omics ", snf_subtype_multiomic,
        " / Phenotype ", snf_subtype_phenotype
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| results: asis

# Render as a collapsible callout instead of a raw message/cat() dump, so a
# long ID list doesn't clutter the report body but is still available to
# readers who want to audit exclusions.
if (length(phenotype_only_dropped) > 0L) {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "::: {{.callout-note collapse=\"true\"}}\n",
    "## {length(phenotype_only_dropped)} participant(s) excluded from this comparison\n\n",
    "These participants have a multi-omics subtype but were excluded from ",
    "phenotype-based clustering due to missing phenotype change score(s):\n\n",
    "{paste(sort(phenotype_only_dropped), collapse = ', ')}\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
}
```

```{r}
snf_classification_comparison |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = cross_classification,
    col = treatment_group,
    label = list(
      cross_classification ~ "Multi-Omics / Phenotype Subtype",
      treatment_group ~ "Treatment Group"
    )
  )
```

## 4.4 Top Phenotype Feature Contributions (NMI)

Each retained clinical domain is an SNF input block. `rankFeaturesByNMI()`
therefore returns NMI scores for the features within each domain-specific
block. The table and plot show the top three features from domains with more
than three measures and the top feature otherwise.

```{r}
#| label: nmi-feature-ranking-phenotype

top_phenotype_features <- rank_phenotype_snf_features(snf_fit_phenotype)

top_phenotype_features |>
  kableExtra::kbl(
    digits = 3,
    caption = paste(
      "Top phenotype features per clinical domain, ranked by NMI with",
      "phenotype subtypes (top 3 for domains with >3 retained measures,",
      "top 1 otherwise)"
    )
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Top phenotype feature NMI — click to enlarge"

top_phenotype_features |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Feature = forcats::fct_reorder(Feature, NMI)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Feature, y = NMI, fill = Domain)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Domain, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Normalized Mutual Information (with phenotype subtypes)",
    title = "Top Phenotype Feature Contributions per Domain"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

# Part 5: Phenotype-Based Similarity Network Fusion with Fixed Cluster Number (k = 3)

This section repeats the multi-domain phenotype SNF analysis from Part 4 with
the same label-free feature selection, domain-wise normalization, and network
fusion steps, but fixes the number of clusters to **`n_clusters = 3`** rather
than using the Eigen-gap-selected value.

```{r}
#| include: false

# Same label-free preprocessing as Part 4 (MAD feature selection, Z-score
# against all subjects), but with n_clusters fixed at 3 rather than
# data-driven (Eigen-gap) selection.
snf_fit_phenotype_k3 <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = phenotype_snf_blocks,
  n_clusters               = 3,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad"
)
```

Cluster number fixed at **k = 3**.

Within each retained clinical domain, up to 100 features are selected by
median absolute deviation without reference to treatment. Each domain block is
Z-scored across all subjects before the domain-specific affinity networks are
fused, keeping subtype discovery label-free.

```{r}
# Reuses `phenotype_clinical_ids` (all participants with complete phenotype
# change scores) defined in Part 4, NOT the 24-participant multi-omics
# `compare_clusters` cohort.
snf_annotations_phenotype_k3 <- annotate_snf_subtypes(
  subtypes = snf_fit_phenotype_k3$subtypes,
  clinical_data = phenotype_clinical_ids,
  id_col = "id"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    snf_subtype_phenotype_k3 = factor(snf_subtype)
  )

snf_annotations_phenotype_k3 |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = unmasked,
    col = snf_subtype_phenotype_k3,
    label = list(
      unmasked ~ "Treatment Group",
      snf_subtype_phenotype_k3 ~ "Phenotype Subtype (k = 3)"
    )
  )
```

## 5.1 Phenotype Subtype Classification from k = 2 to k = 3

This Sankey diagram compares the two phenotype-clustering solutions for the
same complete-case cohort. Each band follows one participant from the k = 2
assignment to the k = 3 assignment. It visualizes how the k = 2 groups split
or overlap when a third subtype is requested; it does not represent change
over time. Subtype numbers are arbitrary cluster labels.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype subtype assignments from k=2 to k=3 - click to enlarge"

phenotype_transition_k2 <- snf_annotations_phenotype |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    `k = 2` = as.character(snf_subtype_phenotype)
  )
phenotype_transition_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_k3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    `k = 3` = as.character(snf_subtype_phenotype_k3)
  )

if (anyDuplicated(phenotype_transition_k2$id) ||
    anyDuplicated(phenotype_transition_k3$id)) {
  stop("Each phenotype classification must contain one row per participant.")
}
if (!setequal(phenotype_transition_k2$id, phenotype_transition_k3$id)) {
  stop("The k = 2 and k = 3 phenotype classifications contain different participants.")
}

phenotype_subtype_sankey_data <- phenotype_transition_k2 |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    phenotype_transition_k3,
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`k = 2`, `k = 3`),
    names_to = "classification",
    values_to = "subtype"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    classification = factor(classification, levels = c("k = 2", "k = 3")),
    subtype = factor(
      subtype,
      levels = c("Subtype 1", "Subtype 2", "Subtype 3")
    )
  )

draw_subtype_sankey(
  sankey_data = phenotype_subtype_sankey_data,
  base_size = 11
)
```

The heatmap displays the domain-specific phenotype change-score blocks used for

SNF cohort uses complete-case filtering (`na.omit()`), so participants with
missing retained phenotype data are excluded rather than imputed.

```{r}

phenotype_subtype_levels_k3 <- phenotype_heatmap_annot_k3[["Phenotype Subtype"]] |>

phenotype_subtype_palette_k3 <- stats::setNames(

phenotype_heatmap_display_k3 <- order_heatmap_rows_by_subtype(

pheatmap::pheatmap(

  color = omics_col_pal,
  annotation_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_k3$annotation,
  annotation_colors = list(
    `Phenotype Subtype` = phenotype_subtype_palette_k3,
    `Treatment Group` = treatment_palette
  ),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  gaps_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_k3$gaps_row,
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize = 10,
  fontsize_row = 9,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Phenotype Changes (Visit 3 - Visit 1), Z-scored (k = 3)"
)
```

## 5.3 Phenotype Similarity Network (k = 3)

The network displays the strongest 5% of participant-to-participant
similarities from the phenotype affinity matrix. Node color identifies the
phenotype-derived subtype, node shape identifies treatment group, and edge
opacity represents similarity strength.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype similarity network (k=3) — click to enlarge"

phenotype_affinity_k3 <- snf_fit_phenotype_k3$fused_network
phenotype_edge_values_k3 <- phenotype_affinity_k3[upper.tri(phenotype_affinity_k3)]
phenotype_edge_threshold_k3 <- stats::quantile(
  phenotype_edge_values_k3,
  probs = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_network_matrix_k3 <- phenotype_affinity_k3
phenotype_network_matrix_k3[
  phenotype_network_matrix_k3 < phenotype_edge_threshold_k3
] <- 0
diag(phenotype_network_matrix_k3) <- 0

phenotype_network_k3 <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  phenotype_network_matrix_k3,
  mode = "undirected",
  weighted = TRUE,
  diag = FALSE
)

snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup <- snf_annotations_phenotype_k3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))

# Drop any network vertices without a matching phenotype-subtype annotation
# so vertex attributes stay aligned with the graph.
phenotype_annotation_idx_k3 <- match(
  igraph::V(phenotype_network_k3)$name,
  snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup$id
)

phenotype_network_dropped_k3 <- igraph::V(phenotype_network_k3)$name[
  is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_k3)
]
if (length(phenotype_network_dropped_k3) > 0L) {
  message(
    "Dropping participant(s) without phenotype subtype annotations from the network (k = 3): ",
    paste(phenotype_network_dropped_k3, collapse = ", ")
  )
  phenotype_network_k3 <- igraph::delete_vertices(
    phenotype_network_k3,
    which(is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_k3))
  )
  phenotype_annotation_idx_k3 <- phenotype_annotation_idx_k3[
    !is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_k3)
  ]
}

phenotype_network_annotations_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup |>
  dplyr::slice(phenotype_annotation_idx_k3)

phenotype_network_k3 <- phenotype_network_k3 |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "phenotype_subtype",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_k3$snf_subtype_phenotype_k3
  ) |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "treatment_group",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_k3$unmasked
  )

set.seed(4328)
fr_layout_k3 <- igraph::layout_with_fr(phenotype_network_k3)
phenotype_network_layout_k3 <- ggnetwork::ggnetwork(
  phenotype_network_k3,
  layout = fr_layout_k3,
  weights = igraph::E(phenotype_network_k3)$weight
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  phenotype_network_layout_k3,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
) +
  ggnetwork::geom_edges(
    ggplot2::aes(linewidth = weight),
    colour = "grey55",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnetwork::geom_nodes(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = phenotype_subtype,
      shape = treatment_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = phenotype_subtype_palette_k3,
    name = "Phenotype Subtype"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(21, 24),
    name = "Treatment Group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black")
    ),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = "grey50")
    )
  ) +
  ggnetwork::theme_blank() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Fused similarity network (k = 3)") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

## 5.4 Multi-Omics and Phenotype Classification Comparison (k = 3)

The two subtype assignments are joined by participant ID and combined into
cross-classified rows. Treatment groups are displayed in columns. Subtype
numbers are arbitrary labels, so equally numbered multi-omic and phenotype
subtypes should not be assumed to represent the same group. The multi-omic
subtypes here are the Part 3 (Eigen-gap-selected) assignments, unchanged;
only the phenotype subtypes are fixed at k = 3.

```{r}
phenotype_classification_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_k3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    snf_subtype_phenotype_k3 = droplevels(factor(snf_subtype_phenotype_k3))
  )

if (anyDuplicated(multiomic_classification$id) ||
    anyDuplicated(phenotype_classification_k3$id)) {
  stop("Each classification must contain one row per participant (k = 3).")
}

phenotype_only_dropped_k3 <- setdiff(
  multiomic_classification$id,
  phenotype_classification_k3$id
)

snf_classification_comparison_k3 <- multiomic_classification |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    phenotype_classification_k3,
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cross_classification = factor(
      paste0(
        "Multi-omics ", snf_subtype_multiomic,
        " / Phenotype ", snf_subtype_phenotype_k3
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| results: asis

if (length(phenotype_only_dropped_k3) > 0L) {
  cat(glue::glue(
    "::: {{.callout-note collapse=\"true\"}}\n",
    "## {length(phenotype_only_dropped_k3)} participant(s) excluded from this comparison\n\n",
    "These participants have a multi-omics subtype but were excluded from ",
    "phenotype-based clustering due to missing phenotype change score(s):\n\n",
    "{paste(sort(phenotype_only_dropped_k3), collapse = ', ')}\n",
    ":::\n"
  ))
}
```

```{r}
snf_classification_comparison_k3 |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = cross_classification,
    col = treatment_group,
    label = list(
      cross_classification ~ "Multi-Omics / Phenotype Subtype (k = 3)",
      treatment_group ~ "Treatment Group"
    )
  )
```

# Part 6: Phenotype Subgroup Analysis - Age 6-11 Years

This section repeats the phenotype analyses from Parts 4 and 5 using only
participants with `age_group == "Age 6-11"`. This is the project field that
records the requested age-group type. All preprocessing, feature selection,
normalization, clustering, and feature-ranking steps are recalculated within
this subgroup. Part 6 uses phenotype-domain blocks only; no multi-omic data or
multi-omic subtype assignments enter these models.

```{r}
#| include: false

age_6_11_group_type <- "Age 6-11"

# Restrict the complete phenotype-change cohort before preprocessing so every
# Part 6 result is estimated solely from participants aged 6–11 years.
phenotype_snf_data_age_6_11 <- phenotype_snf_data |>
  dplyr::filter(age_group == age_6_11_group_type)

if (nrow(phenotype_snf_data_age_6_11) < 3L) {
  stop("At least three complete phenotype records are required for the age 6–11 subgroup analysis.")
}

phenotype_snf_blocks_age_6_11 <- make_phenotype_snf_blocks(
  data = phenotype_snf_data_age_6_11,
  domains = phenotype_domains
)
```

## Phenotype-Based Similarity Network Fusion

Within the age 6-11 subgroup, phenotype change scores are represented as one
input block per retained clinical domain. `run_snf_subtypes()` constructs an
affinity matrix for each domain and fuses the resulting networks before
spectral clustering; feature selection and normalization remain label-free.

```{r}
#| include: false

# SAP Step 2: retain up to the top 100 features within each clinical-domain
# block by dispersion (MAD), with no reference to treatment group.
# SAP Step 3: normalize each domain block against all subjects so treatment
# assignment never enters the clustering input through centering or scaling.
# SAP Step 4: preliminary SNF to obtain a fused network for cluster estimation
snf_prelim_phenotype_age_6_11 <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = phenotype_snf_blocks_age_6_11,
  n_clusters               = 2,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad"
)

# SAP Step 4: data-driven cluster number selection (Eigen-gap criterion)
n_clust_est_phenotype_age_6_11         <- SNFtool::estimateNumberOfClustersGivenGraph(
  W = snf_prelim_phenotype_age_6_11$fused_network, NUMC = 2:8
)
n_clusters_selected_phenotype_age_6_11 <- n_clust_est_phenotype_age_6_11[[1]]

# Final run with data-selected number of clusters
snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11 <- run_snf_subtypes(
  omics                    = phenotype_snf_blocks_age_6_11,
  n_clusters               = n_clusters_selected_phenotype_age_6_11,
  K                        = 10,
  t                        = 20,
  top_features             = 100,
  feature_selection_method = "mad"
)
```

The Eigen-gap criterion suggests **`r n_clusters_selected_phenotype_age_6_11`**
cluster(s) (Rotation cost criterion: `r n_clust_est_phenotype_age_6_11[[2]]`).
Within each retained clinical domain, up to 100 features are selected by
median absolute deviation without reference to treatment. Each domain block is
Z-scored across all subjects before the domain-specific affinity networks are
fused, keeping subtype discovery label-free.

```{r}
# Join phenotype subtypes to the complete age 6-11 phenotype-change cohort.
# `phenotype_snf_data_age_6_11` has already been restricted before clustering.
phenotype_clinical_ids_age_6_11 <- phenotype_snf_data_age_6_11 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = fxs_sts_id,
    unmasked = Treatment
  )

snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11 <- annotate_snf_subtypes(
  subtypes = snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11$subtypes,
  clinical_data = phenotype_clinical_ids_age_6_11,
  id_col = "id"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    snf_subtype_phenotype = factor(snf_subtype)
  )

snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11 |>
  gtsummary::tbl_cross(
    row = unmasked,
    col = snf_subtype_phenotype,
    label = list(
      unmasked ~ "Treatment Group",
      snf_subtype_phenotype ~ "Phenotype Subtype (Age 6-11)"
    )
  )
```

### Phenotype Change Heatmap by Subgroup

The heatmap displays the domain-specific phenotype change-score blocks used for
SNF. Values are standardized within outcome across participants. The phenotype
SNF cohort uses complete-case filtering (`na.omit()`), so participants with
missing retained phenotype data are excluded rather than imputed.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

)

  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
  dplyr::slice(match(rownames(phenotype_heatmap_matrix_age_6_11), id))

  droplevels() |>
  levels()
phenotype_subtype_palette_age_6_11 <- stats::setNames(
  scales::hue_pal()(length(phenotype_subtype_levels_age_6_11)),
  phenotype_subtype_levels_age_6_11
)
phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11 <- order_heatmap_rows_by_subtype(
  mat = phenotype_heatmap_matrix_age_6_11,
  annotation = phenotype_heatmap_annot_age_6_11,
  subtype_col = "Phenotype Subtype"
)

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11$matrix,
  color = omics_col_pal,
  annotation_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11$annotation,
  annotation_colors = list(

  ),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  gaps_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11$gaps_row,
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize = 10,
  fontsize_row = 9,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Phenotype Changes (Visit 3 - Visit 1), Z-scored - Age 6-11"
)
```

### Phenotype Similarity Network

The network displays the strongest 5% of participant-to-participant
similarities from the phenotype affinity matrix. Node color identifies the
phenotype-derived subtype, node shape identifies treatment group, and edge
opacity represents similarity strength.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype similarity network — click to enlarge"

phenotype_affinity_age_6_11 <- snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11$fused_network
phenotype_edge_values_age_6_11 <- phenotype_affinity_age_6_11[upper.tri(phenotype_affinity_age_6_11)]
phenotype_edge_threshold_age_6_11 <- stats::quantile(
  phenotype_edge_values_age_6_11,
  probs = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11 <- phenotype_affinity_age_6_11
phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11[
  phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11 < phenotype_edge_threshold_age_6_11
] <- 0
diag(phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11) <- 0

phenotype_network_age_6_11 <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11,
  mode = "undirected",
  weighted = TRUE,
  diag = FALSE
)

snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup <- snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))

# `dplyr::slice(match(...))` silently drops rows for any unmatched vertex
# name instead of producing an NA row, which would desync the annotations
# from the graph's vertex count. Explicitly drop any network vertices that
# lack a matching phenotype-subtype annotation (e.g. participants excluded
# from phenotype-based clustering by `na.omit()` upstream) before assigning
# vertex attributes, so the two stay aligned.
phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11 <- match(
  igraph::V(phenotype_network_age_6_11)$name,
  snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup$id
)

phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11 <- igraph::V(phenotype_network_age_6_11)$name[
  is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11)
]
if (length(phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11) > 0L) {
  message(
    "Dropping participant(s) without phenotype subtype annotations from the network: ",
    paste(phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11, collapse = ", ")
  )
  phenotype_network_age_6_11 <- igraph::delete_vertices(
    phenotype_network_age_6_11,
    which(is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11))
  )
  phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11 <- phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11[
    !is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11)
  ]
}

phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_lookup |>
  dplyr::slice(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11)

phenotype_network_age_6_11 <- phenotype_network_age_6_11 |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "phenotype_subtype",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11$snf_subtype_phenotype
  ) |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "treatment_group",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11$unmasked
  )

set.seed(4328)
fr_layout_age_6_11 <- igraph::layout_with_fr(phenotype_network_age_6_11)
phenotype_network_layout_age_6_11 <- ggnetwork::ggnetwork(
  phenotype_network_age_6_11,
  layout = fr_layout_age_6_11,
  weights = igraph::E(phenotype_network_age_6_11)$weight
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  phenotype_network_layout_age_6_11,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
) +
  ggnetwork::geom_edges(
    ggplot2::aes(linewidth = weight),
    colour = "grey55",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnetwork::geom_nodes(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = phenotype_subtype,
      shape = treatment_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = phenotype_subtype_palette_age_6_11,
    name = "Phenotype Subtype"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(21, 24),
    name = "Treatment Group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black")
    ),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = "grey50")
    )
  ) +
  ggnetwork::theme_blank() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Phenotype similarity network - Age 6-11") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
```

## Phenotype-Based Similarity Network Fusion with Fixed Cluster Number (k = 3)

This section repeats the age 6-11 multi-domain phenotype SNF analysis with the

the number of clusters to **`n_clusters = 3`**.

```{r}
#| include: false

# Same label-free preprocessing as Part 4 (MAD feature selection, Z-score
# against all subjects), but with n_clusters fixed at 3 rather than
# data-driven (Eigen-gap) selection.
snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11_k3 <- run_snf_subtypes(

)
```

Cluster number fixed at **k = 3**.

Within each retained clinical domain, up to 100 features are selected by
median absolute deviation without reference to treatment. Each domain block is
Z-scored across all subjects before the domain-specific affinity networks are
fused, keeping subtype discovery label-free.

```{r}
# Reuse the age 6-11 phenotype cohort defined above.
snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11_k3 <- annotate_snf_subtypes(
  subtypes = snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11_k3$subtypes,
  clinical_data = phenotype_clinical_ids_age_6_11,

) |>

    )

```

### Phenotype Subtype Classification from k = 2 to k = 3

This Sankey diagram compares the two phenotype-clustering solutions within the
same complete-case age 6-11 cohort. Each band follows one participant from the
k = 2 assignment to the k = 3 assignment. It visualizes how the k = 2 groups
split or overlap when a third subtype is requested; it does not represent
change over time. Subtype numbers are arbitrary cluster labels.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Age 6-11 phenotype subtype assignments from k=2 to k=3 - click to enlarge"

if (length(n_clusters_selected_phenotype_age_6_11) != 1L ||
    as.integer(n_clusters_selected_phenotype_age_6_11) != 2L) {
  stop(
    "The age 6-11 classification Sankey requires the data-selected solution to have k = 2."
  )
}

phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k2 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    `k = 2` = as.character(snf_subtype_phenotype)
  )
phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11_k3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.character(id),
    `k = 3` = as.character(snf_subtype_phenotype_k3)
  )

if (anyDuplicated(phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k2$id) ||
    anyDuplicated(phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k3$id)) {
  stop("Each age 6-11 phenotype classification must contain one row per participant.")
}
if (!setequal(
  phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k2$id,
  phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k3$id
)) {
  stop(
    "The k = 2 and k = 3 age 6-11 phenotype classifications contain different participants."
  )
}

phenotype_subtype_sankey_data_age_6_11 <-
  phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k2 |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    phenotype_transition_age_6_11_k3,
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`k = 2`, `k = 3`),
    names_to = "classification",
    values_to = "subtype"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    classification = factor(classification, levels = c("k = 2", "k = 3")),
    subtype = factor(
      subtype,
      levels = c("Subtype 1", "Subtype 2", "Subtype 3")
    )
  )

draw_subtype_sankey(
  sankey_data = phenotype_subtype_sankey_data_age_6_11,
  base_size = 11,
  plot_title = paste(
    "Phenotype subtype assignments: k = 2 versus k = 3",
    "Age 6-11",
    sep = " - "
  )
)
```

### Phenotype Change Heatmap by Subgroup (k = 3)

The heatmap displays the domain-specific phenotype change-score blocks used for
SNF. Values are standardized within outcome across participants. The phenotype
SNF cohort uses complete-case filtering (`na.omit()`), so participants with
missing retained phenotype data are excluded rather than imputed.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype change heatmap (k=3) - click to enlarge"

phenotype_heatmap_matrix_age_6_11_k3 <- combine_phenotype_snf_blocks(
  snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11_k3$processed_omics
)

phenotype_heatmap_annotations_age_6_11_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11_k3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id)) |>
  dplyr::slice(match(rownames(phenotype_heatmap_matrix_age_6_11_k3), id))

if (anyNA(phenotype_heatmap_annotations_age_6_11_k3$id)) {
  stop("Phenotype heatmap annotations are missing for at least one participant (k = 3).")
}

phenotype_heatmap_annot_age_6_11_k3 <- data.frame(
  `Phenotype Subtype` = phenotype_heatmap_annotations_age_6_11_k3$snf_subtype_phenotype_k3,
  `Treatment Group` = phenotype_heatmap_annotations_age_6_11_k3$unmasked,
  row.names = phenotype_heatmap_annotations_age_6_11_k3$id,
  check.names = FALSE
)

phenotype_subtype_levels_age_6_11_k3 <- phenotype_heatmap_annot_age_6_11_k3[["Phenotype Subtype"]] |>
  droplevels() |>
  levels()
phenotype_subtype_palette_age_6_11_k3 <- stats::setNames(
  scales::hue_pal()(length(phenotype_subtype_levels_age_6_11_k3)),
  phenotype_subtype_levels_age_6_11_k3
)
phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11_k3 <- order_heatmap_rows_by_subtype(
  mat = phenotype_heatmap_matrix_age_6_11_k3,
  annotation = phenotype_heatmap_annot_age_6_11_k3,
  subtype_col = "Phenotype Subtype"
)

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11_k3$matrix,
  color = omics_col_pal,
  annotation_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11_k3$annotation,
  annotation_colors = list(
    `Phenotype Subtype` = phenotype_subtype_palette_age_6_11_k3,
    `Treatment Group` = treatment_palette
  ),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  gaps_row = phenotype_heatmap_display_age_6_11_k3$gaps_row,
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize = 10,
  fontsize_row = 9,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Phenotype Changes (Visit 3 - Visit 1), Z-scored - Age 6-11 (k = 3)"
)
```

### Phenotype Similarity Network (k = 3)

The network displays the strongest 5% of participant-to-participant
similarities from the phenotype affinity matrix. Node color identifies the
phenotype-derived subtype, node shape identifies treatment group, and edge
opacity represents similarity strength.

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 150
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Phenotype similarity network (k=3) — click to enlarge"

phenotype_affinity_age_6_11_k3 <- snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11_k3$fused_network
phenotype_edge_values_age_6_11_k3 <- phenotype_affinity_age_6_11_k3[upper.tri(phenotype_affinity_age_6_11_k3)]
phenotype_edge_threshold_age_6_11_k3 <- stats::quantile(
  phenotype_edge_values_age_6_11_k3,
  probs = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11_k3 <- phenotype_affinity_age_6_11_k3
phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11_k3[
  phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11_k3 < phenotype_edge_threshold_age_6_11_k3
] <- 0
diag(phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11_k3) <- 0

phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3 <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  phenotype_network_matrix_age_6_11_k3,
  mode = "undirected",
  weighted = TRUE,
  diag = FALSE
)

snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup <- snf_annotations_phenotype_age_6_11_k3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))

# Drop any network vertices without a matching phenotype-subtype annotation
# so vertex attributes stay aligned with the graph.
phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3 <- match(
  igraph::V(phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3)$name,
  snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup$id
)

phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11_k3 <- igraph::V(phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3)$name[
  is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3)
]
if (length(phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11_k3) > 0L) {
  message(
    "Dropping participant(s) without phenotype subtype annotations from the network (k = 3): ",
    paste(phenotype_network_dropped_age_6_11_k3, collapse = ", ")
  )
  phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3 <- igraph::delete_vertices(
    phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3,
    which(is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3))
  )
  phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3 <- phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3[
    !is.na(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3)
  ]
}

phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11_k3 <- snf_annotations_phenotype_k3_lookup |>
  dplyr::slice(phenotype_annotation_idx_age_6_11_k3)

phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3 <- phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3 |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "phenotype_subtype",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11_k3$snf_subtype_phenotype_k3
  ) |>
  igraph::set_vertex_attr(
    name = "treatment_group",
    value = phenotype_network_annotations_age_6_11_k3$unmasked
  )

set.seed(4328)
fr_layout_age_6_11_k3 <- igraph::layout_with_fr(phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3)
phenotype_network_layout_age_6_11_k3 <- ggnetwork::ggnetwork(
  phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3,
  layout = fr_layout_age_6_11_k3,
  weights = igraph::E(phenotype_network_age_6_11_k3)$weight
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  phenotype_network_layout_age_6_11_k3,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
) +
  ggnetwork::geom_edges(
    ggplot2::aes(linewidth = weight),
    colour = "grey55",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggnetwork::geom_nodes(
    ggplot2::aes(
      fill = phenotype_subtype,
      shape = treatment_group
    ),
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 7,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = phenotype_subtype_palette_age_6_11_k3,
    name = "Phenotype Subtype"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(21, 24),
    name = "Treatment Group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black")
    ),
    shape = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(fill = "grey50")
    )
  ) +
  ggnetwork::theme_blank() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Phenotype similarity network - Age 6-11 (k = 3)") +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

### Top Phenotype Feature Contributions (NMI, k = 3)

As above, each retained clinical domain is an SNF block in the age 6-11
analysis. NMI scores are calculated within those domain-specific blocks
against the k = 3 phenotype subtypes.

```{r}
#| label: nmi-feature-ranking-phenotype-age-6-11-k3

top_phenotype_features_age_6_11_k3 <- rank_phenotype_snf_features(snf_fit_phenotype_age_6_11_k3)

top_phenotype_features_age_6_11_k3 |>
  kableExtra::kbl(
    digits = 3,
    caption = paste(
      "Top phenotype features per clinical domain, ranked by NMI with",
      "k = 3 age 6-11 phenotype subtypes (top 3 for domains with >3 retained measures,",
      "top 1 otherwise)"
    )
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-dpi: 96
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| lightbox:
#|   description: "Top phenotype feature NMI (k=3) — click to enlarge"

top_phenotype_features_age_6_11_k3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Feature = forcats::fct_reorder(Feature, NMI)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Feature, y = NMI, fill = Domain)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Domain, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Normalized Mutual Information (with age 6-11 k = 3 phenotype subtypes)",
    title = "Top Phenotype Feature Contributions per Domain - Age 6-11 (k = 3)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```
